title: Details of the Don't You Know session
summary: Personnel of the December 1953 session and recording at WDSU or Cosmo's studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well I want to talk about his, do you remember that first recording with Ray? The one with, with, called Don't You Know. Yeah, Don't You Know. Yeah. But now I forgot the name of the other tunes. Well Ray's Blues and Nobody Cares and Mr. Charles' Blues. Those are the four tracks for, I think Don't You Know was the mix, the song that got any play. Yeah. It got airplay. I've never heard of those other songs.
I know I've got them someplace, we can probably dig them out. But, but don't you, the song Don't You Know was a big one. Yeah. And, yeah, you were on trumpet and Frank Mitchell was on trumpet.
Joe Tillman, Tillman played, tenor, Lloyd Lambert played bass. Right. And, Warren Bell. Yeah, Warren was on there in baritone.
Yeah, baritone. Baritone. And, Gerald O'Neal.
Oh yeah, I forgot about that, he's a wonderful alto player. O'Neal Gerald. O'Neal Gerald. Okay.

And, and Oscar Moore. A drummer. A drummer. Oscar Moore. Yeah. A drummer. A drummer. Oscar Moore. Yeah, this was December 4th, 1953. Was that his first recording? No, first recording for Atlantic but his first for Atlantic.
Because he did one thing, I think that was Atlantic, it could have been me, it should have been me with this real fine chick.
I'm just looking at a list here. I'm wondering if it's something you did and it wasn't released, or something. I have to go back and look.
Now this other thing with the big band, You Are My Sunshine, I was on that too, I made that.
What song called You Are My Sunshine?
Yeah, You Are My Sunshine. He did that with the big band.
That must have been later, I think that was later in his career. Now I was wondering, on this, on the You Know song, was that done, I've got a note here that it was done at WDSU.
Okay. Yeah. Did you, usually did you go to record at Cosmo? Oh yeah.
Cosmo Matassa's studio. I think there was somebody else recording at Cosmo at that time, because he did a lot of recording at his studio. So yeah, so that was the reason that you didn't work at WDSU.
I'm more than sure that's what the reason. Yeah. I'm more than sure that's what the reason. I'm just looking over recordings now.
